summary: Iter212 re-test after main-agent fix to `_post_to_accounting` idempotency guard + `update_payslip` re-aggregation on already-paid edits. Both fixes verified in code. Ran 16 pytest cases (added 4 iter212 regressions: donation single-JE, expense approve single-JE, single-payslip single-JE, edit-already-paid re-post). Result: 12 passed, 2 failed, 2 skipped. The two failures pinpoint a SECOND, related critical bug that the iter211 fix did NOT fully close: `_reverse_auto_posted_je` in financial.py line 236 also lacks the `is_reversed:{$ne:True}` filter — after the first reversal, its `find_one` keeps picking up the OLD reversed entry, returns 0, and then `_post_to_accounting` (which now DOES filter is_reversed) still short-circuits on the STILL-active most-recent JE. Net effect: after the SECOND aggregation update, the ledger's active payroll JE is frozen and every further re-aggregation is a no-op. Confirmed via DB: source_id='payroll_loc_001_2026-07-04' has only 2 entries (je_45fdbc2571 total=470000 is_reversed=true; je_f8f1522fab total=3,970,000 active) while the aggregate expense doc = 6,003,330 across 20 staff.

critical.issue: find_one({auto_generated_from, source_id}) has no `is_reversed:{$ne:True}` filter. After the FIRST reversal+repost cycle, Mongo returns the OLDER (already-reversed) entry — the function's early `if entry.get('is_reversed'): return 0` bails out, so the currently-active latest JE is NEVER reversed. Then _post_to_accounting sees that still-active entry and short-circuits. Result: from the THIRD payslip onward (same location, same day), the ledger's active payroll JE is frozen at the amount posted after payslip #2 — every subsequent salary paid is silently dropped from the ledger. Same-shape bug as iter211 but on the reversal side. RCA verified via direct DB query. FIX: change line 236 to `find_one({'auto_generated_from':source_kind,'source_id':source_id,'is_reversed':{'$ne':True}})`. This is a 1-line change; symmetric to the iter211 idempotency-guard fix.

minor.issue: Sorted by date desc (not created_at desc), so entries with old `date` values (e.g. tests using 2025-02-16) are pushed past limit=500 even when just created. Tests should always pass `date_from=today` or the API should offer sort=created_at.

action_items: FIX CRITICAL (financial.py line 236 in _reverse_auto_posted_je): add `'is_reversed':{'$ne':True}` to the find_one filter so the reversal targets the CURRENTLY-active JE, not the oldest already-reversed one. Without this, iter211's _post_to_accounting fix is only half a fix — the reversal step still misses so subsequent re-aggregations no-op.
OPTIONAL hardening: in _aggregate_payroll_expense, verify the reverse step by counting active JEs before/after (should be 0 immediately after reverse, then 1 after re-post). Log a warning if not.
critical_code_review_comments: financial.py::_reverse_auto_posted_je is a mirror-image of the same bug just fixed in _post_to_accounting — it selects an entry by (auto_generated_from, source_id) but doesn't disambiguate active-vs-reversed. Every reverse+repost aggregate flow (payroll, and any future donation/expense edit that reverses) is broken past the 2nd cycle.

test_single_payslip_paid_posts_exactly_one_active_je passes because it only asserts len(active)==1 — but doesn't verify total_debit matches aggregate amount. Recommend strengthening this assertion (or keeping it as a distinct 'no duplicate JE' test and adding a separate 'amount matches' one).
iter211 fix was verified in place (financial.py line 321 correctly filters is_reversed). hr.py update_payslip re-aggregation on already-paid edit is also verified in place (line 642).

context_for_next_testing_agent: One-line fix expected in _reverse_auto_posted_je (add is_reversed:{$ne:true} to its find_one, exactly like the iter211 fix in _post_to_accounting). After the fix, re-run only the two failing tests: `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iter211_payroll_je_and_repair.py::TestPayrollAggregation::test_two_payslips_same_day_aggregate_and_reverse_prior_je /app/backend/tests/test_iter211_payroll_je_and_repair.py::TestNoDoublePosting::test_edit_already_paid_payslip_updates_ledger -v`. Note the aggregate expense payroll_loc_001_YYYY-MM-DD is deterministic per day — tests already assert amount>=net1+net2 and 'active JE == aggregate' so they're resilient across sessions. Existing broken state: payroll_loc_001_2026-07-04 aggregate=6,003,330 but active JE=3,970,000 (stale since 12:20:31 UTC) — will remain broken until the fix is applied and a new payslip is paid to trigger a fresh reverse+repost cycle.
rca of the issue: SEQUENCE (verified via DB): (A) 1st payslip paid — expense doc created, JE1 posted (source_id=payroll_loc_001_YYYY-MM-DD). (B) 2nd payslip paid — _aggregate_payroll_expense updates expense.amount, calls _reverse_auto_posted_je which find_one's JE1 (active), reverses it (JE1.is_reversed=true), then _post_to_accounting posts JE2 (active). ✅ Works. (C) 3rd (and every later) payslip paid — _aggregate_payroll_expense updates expense.amount, calls _reverse_auto_posted_je which now find_one's *JE1* FIRST (returned before JE2 because Mongo natural order = insertion order), sees is_reversed=true, returns 0 (no reversal). Then _post_to_accounting runs its idempotency guard `find_one({...,'is_reversed':{'$ne':True}})` — matches JE2 (still active) → returns early. No new JE posted. ❌ Broken. Fix: `_reverse_auto_posted_je` must also filter `is_reversed:{$ne:True}` so it targets JE2 for reversal, allowing _post_to_accounting to post JE3.
